title: Save your demo account history as a statement
summary: Save your [[demo-account]] trade history from MetaTrader as an HTML report, then import it in the Journal. The export option and its name depend on your app version and platform.

steps.text: Check you are logged in to your demo account, not a real one. Only import demo statements.

On your phone, open the History tab and set the period so it covers your demo trades. Look for an option to save, share or export a report. It depends on your app version: many phone versions do not have one.
If your phone app cannot export the history, log in to the same demo account in the desktop MetaTrader terminal on a computer.
In the desktop terminal, open the history list in the bottom panel.
steps.mt4: Open the Terminal window and choose the Account History tab.
steps.mt5: Open the Toolbox window and choose the History tab.

steps.text: Right-click inside the history list and choose a period that covers all your demo trades.
Right-click again and look for the report option. The exact name depends on your version.
steps.mt4: It is usually called "Save as Report" or "Save as Detailed Report".
steps.mt5: It is usually called "Report", with a choice of formats.

steps.text: Choose HTML if you are offered a format. The Journal import reads HTML statements.
Save the file, then move it to your phone, for example by sending it to yourself. Keep it private: it shows your account number and history.
In TradeLab, open the Journal and choose the option to import an MT statement. Pick the file.
Check the preview: the number of closed trades and their prices should match your MetaTrader history. Trades already imported are skipped.
Confirm the import. Then open each imported trade, add a chart screenshot, and complete the review.

afterQuestions.prompt: Someone in a chat offers to export your statement for you if you send your MetaTrader login. What do you do?

options.text: Send it; it is only a demo account
options.explanation: No: never share MetaTrader logins. It builds a habit scammers rely on.
Right: never share your login, demo or real.

afterQuestions.prompt: Your phone app has no option to save a report. What can you do?

options.text: Export it from the desktop terminal, or add your trades by hand with screenshots
options.explanation: Right: on some app versions the desktop terminal is the way to export.

options.text: Give up on journaling these trades
options.explanation: No: you can still log them by hand in the Journal.
